newsitem.title: USA: Bank error in bearer bonds leads to SEC action.
newsitem.headline: Bank error in bearer bonds leads to SEC action.

text.p: An inadvertent error by a U.S. bank involving municipal bearer bonds has resulted in the Securities and Exchange Commission filing securities fraud charges against a former broker with David A. Noyes & Co.

The SEC said on Wednesday that it filed a civil action on October 28 in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Illinois against Frank Colin, who worked for Noyes from about March 1994 through August 1995.

Toward the end of his term at Indianapolis-based Noyes, the SEC alleged in a complaint that Colin secretly transferred $1.6 million in securities and funds from a customer's account to Citicorp Investment Services.
Posing as the customer, Colin sold the securities, purchased municipal bearer bonds with some of the proceeds and placed the proceeds in the new Citicorp account, SEC said.
But he was caught when Citicorp mistakenly put the bonds in the customer's name and then delayed delivery of the bonds, an SEC enforcement attorney told Reuters.
A "bearer bond" does not carry the name of the bondholder, so it can easily be redeemed at a bank.
"Somehow in the course of the registration process, Citicorp discovered" the problem, the attorney said.
The complaint says Colin misappropriated about $835,000 of the customer's funds. SEC is asking that Colin "disgorge" the funds, including interest.
Earlier this year, Colin was convicted of criminal charges brought by the U.S. Attorney for the Northern District of Illinois. He is awaiting sentencing.
